title: Cook console copies the whole 2000-line buffer twice per log line
body:
## Summary
Every `log` event allocates a new copy of the retained log buffer (and a second at the cap), and every render re-filters the full buffer, so a long cook does O(n) work per line.

## Description
`appendCookLog` (`src/components/modules/game-systems/CookProgress/helpers.ts:34`) does `[...prev, entry]` and, once at `MAX_LOG_LINES` (2000, `src/components/modules/game-systems/CookProgress/constants.ts:18`), a `slice` - two arrays of up to 2000 entries per line. `displayedLines` (`src/components/modules/game-systems/CookProgress/useCookProgress.ts:208`) re-filters the whole buffer whenever `logs` changes, i.e. once per line, and `errorRows` rescans it again. The comment at `useCookProgress.ts:44` claims the tallies are O(1), which they are, but the buffer itself is not. RunUAT emits thousands of lines; fixed looks like a ring buffer or chunked append plus a batched (rAF) flush of state so the console renders at most once per frame.

## Flow
- build a vitest bench driving 5000 `log` events through `driveCookStream` handlers into `useCookProgress` (renderHook)
- measure total ms and allocations on base
- replace the append with a ring buffer / batch flush per animation frame
- re-run the same bench; keep the existing appendCookLog cap tests green

## Expected impact
Lower main-thread time during long cooks (the console stays responsive while tailing). Could break: the facet tallies' trim-mirroring logic, which assumes one append per state update.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - less work per streamed log line
Before: 2 array copies of up to 2000 entries + 2 full-buffer scans per line (read from code; not timed)
After: predicted O(1) append and <=1 render per frame
Method: simulation - no bench instrument exists in the tree and building it plus the change is M
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: vitest bench: renderHook(useCookProgress) fed 5000 log events via a stubbed stream; total ms + render count, base vs ring-buffer arm

title: Smoke-test 'observing ~25s' label is a hand-copied copy of the server window
body:
## Summary
The SmokeTest panel prints a hardcoded `~25s` observe window that only matches the server by coincidence of two separate constants.

## Description
`OBSERVE_LABEL_MS = 25` (`src/components/modules/game-systems/SmokeTest.tsx:37`) - named ms, holds seconds - drives the running label at `SmokeTest.tsx:103`. The real window is `DEFAULT_OBSERVE_MS = 25_000` in `src/lib/packaging/smoke-test.ts:74`, and the route accepts a clamped `observeMs` override (`src/app/api/packaging/smoke-test/route.ts:73`). Two implementations of one number; change either and the panel lies. Fixed looks like one exported client-safe constant (or the route echoing the window it will use) that the label reads.

## Flow
- change DEFAULT_OBSERVE_MS to 40_000 -> panel still says ~25s
- fix: export the default from a client-safe module and derive the label from it
- test: label text contains the derived seconds

## Expected impact
The operator's wait estimate stays true when the window is tuned. Could break: nothing user-visible today (values agree).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for the observe window
Before: 2 hand-maintained constants (SmokeTest.tsx:37, smoke-test.ts:74), agreeing today
After: 1 source, label derived
Method: simulation - smoke-test.ts is outside this context's paths (lib/packaging), so the shared constant cannot be moved this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: test that sets the exported default to a different value and asserts the SmokeTest running label shows it (seed red on the hardcoded 25)

title: Pre-flight error banner is shared by all checks and wiped by any re-run
body:
## Summary
PreflightPanel keeps ONE `error` string for five check kinds: it does not say which check failed, and starting any other check erases it.

## Description
`runCheck` calls `setError(null)` at dispatch (`src/components/modules/game-systems/PreflightPanel.tsx:192`) and `setError(res.error)` on failure (`PreflightPanel.tsx:211`). A Shipping build-verify that fails with an HTTP error (minutes of work) is erased the moment the user presses Re-run for the fast checks, and while shown it carries no check name, so the tile it belongs to still reads NOT RUN with no reason. Fixed looks like a per-kind error map rendered on that kind's tile.

## Flow
- press Build verify -> Shipping; the route fails (HTTP 500)
- banner shows the raw error, unattributed
- press Re-run -> banner disappears; the Shipping tile says 'Not run - no verdict' with no trace of the failure

## Expected impact
A failed slow check stays visible on its own tile until re-run. Could break: PreflightCoverage tests that assert the single pof-preflight-error testid.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a check failure stays attributed and visible
Before: 1 shared error slot for 5 kinds; erased by 4 of 4 other dispatches (walked from code)
After: predicted per-kind slot, 0 erasures by other kinds
Method: simulation - walked the three dispatch paths (auto-run, Re-run, Package requestedChecks); test not built this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: PreflightPanel test: build-verify-shipping POST returns 500, then click Re-run; assert the shipping tile still names the failure (seed red on base)

title: Cook settings switches show no keyboard focus
body:
## Summary
The Toggle switches in CookSettingsPanel hide the real checkbox with `sr-only` and draw a track with no focus style, so a keyboard user cannot see which switch has focus.

## Description
`Toggle` (`src/components/modules/game-systems/CookSettingsPanel.tsx` Toggle component, input `className="sr-only"`) renders a visual track div with no `peer-focus-visible` ring; the repo has a shared `.focus-ring` token (reference_focus_ring_token) used elsewhere in this context (NightlyBuildScheduler inputs). 7 switches on the profile editor are affected. Fixed: `peer` on the input and `peer-focus-visible:` ring classes (or the focus-ring token) on the track.

## Flow
- open Pipeline tab -> edit a profile -> Tab through cook settings
- focus moves onto the hidden checkboxes; nothing on screen changes

## Expected impact
Keyboard users can operate the cook settings (WCAG 2.4.7). Could break: nothing functional.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - visible focus on 7 switches
Before: 0 of 7 switches render a focus indicator (no focus class on the track)
After: 7 of 7
Method: simulation - jsdom has no :focus-visible rendering; a class-presence test is the reachable instrument but pins classes, not visibility
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/game-systems/CookSettingsPanel.tsx Toggle: <input type="checkbox" ... className="sr-only" /> followed by a track <div> with no focus classes
instrument: Playwright focus screenshot of the profile editor switches, or a test asserting the track carries the shared focus-ring peer class

title: Nightly time field POSTs on every segment edit, including an empty value
body:
## Summary
The Scheduled Builds time input saves on every `change`, so editing hours then minutes fires two writes and clearing the field POSTs `time: ''`.

## Description
`onChange={(e) => save({ time: e.target.value })}` (`src/components/modules/game-systems/NightlyBuildScheduler.tsx` time input). A native time input emits `''` while a segment is cleared and a new value per segment; each becomes a server write (and a refresh GET). The server's `parseTimeOfDay` (`src/lib/packaging/build-scheduler.ts:43`) rejects malformed times, which is now surfaced as 'Save failed' (commit 2bbe3502) - but the user sees an error for a half-typed value. Fixed: hold a draft, save on blur/Enter only when `parseTimeOfDay(draft)` is non-null (same pattern the Gate Notifications URL field uses).

## Flow
- focus the time field, clear the hour -> POST time '' -> 'Save failed'
- type 03 -> POST; tab to minutes, type 30 -> POST

## Expected impact
One write per finished edit, no spurious errors. Could break: the existing test that saves on toggle (unaffected) - nothing else reads the time draft.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one valid write per time edit
Before: 1 POST per change event, including empty values (read from code)
After: predicted 1 POST per committed valid time
Method: simulation - build-scheduler.ts parse helper is outside this context's paths only as an import; test not built this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/game-systems/NightlyBuildScheduler.tsx time input: onChange={(e) => save({ time: e.target.value })}
src/lib/packaging/build-scheduler.ts:43 parseTimeOfDay strict HH:MM
instrument: NightlyBuildScheduler test: fireEvent.change(time, '') then '03:30' then blur; assert exactly one save POST with time '03:30' (seed red on base: 2 POSTs incl. '')
